title: अंश ३ · अध्याय ६

items.text:
सामवेदतरोः शाशा व्यासशिष्यः स जैमिनिः ।
क्रमेण येन मैत्रेय! बिभेद श्वृणु तन्मम ।। १ ।।
items.tr:
sāmavedataroḥ śāśā vyāsaśiṣyaḥ sa jaiminiḥ |
krameṇa yena maitreya! bibheda śvṛṇu tanmama || 1 ||

items.text:
सुमन्तुस्तस्य पुत्रोऽभूत् सुकर्मास्याप्यभूत् सुतः ।
अधीतवन्तावेकैकां संहितां तौ महामुनी ।। २ ।।
items.tr:
sumantustasya putro'bhūt sukarmāsyāpyabhūt sutaḥ |
adhītavantāvekaikāṃ saṃhitāṃ tau mahāmunī || 2 ||

items.text:
साहस्त्रं संहिताभेदं सुकर्मा तत्सुतस्ततः ।
चकार तञ्च तिच्छिष्यौ जगृहाते महामती ।। ३ ।।
items.tr:
sāhastraṃ saṃhitābhedaṃ sukarmā tatsutastataḥ |
cakāra tañca ticchiṣyau jagṛhāte mahāmatī || 3 ||

items.text:
हिरण्यनाभः कौशल्यः पौष्पिञ्जिश्व द्रिजोत्तम ।
उदीच्यसामगाः शिष्यास्तेब्यः पञ्चदशा स्मृताः ।। ४ ।।
items.tr:
hiraṇyanābhaḥ kauśalyaḥ pauṣpiñjiśva drijottama |
udīcyasāmagāḥ śiṣyāstebyaḥ pañcadaśā smṛtāḥ || 4 ||

items.text:
हिरणयनाभात् तावत्यः संहिता यैर्द्रिजोत्तमैः ।
गृहीतास्तेऽपि चोच्यन्ते पण्डितैः प्राच्यसामगाः ।। ५ ।।
items.tr:
hiraṇayanābhāt tāvatyaḥ saṃhitā yairdrijottamaiḥ |
gṛhītāste'pi cocyante paṇḍitaiḥ prācyasāmagāḥ || 5 ||

items.text:
लोकाक्षिः कुथमिश्चैव कुसीदिर्लाङ्गलिस्तथा ।
पौष्पिञ्जिशिष्यास्तद्भदैः संहिता बहूलीकृताः ।। ६ ।।
items.tr:
lokākṣiḥ kuthamiścaiva kusīdirlāṅgalistathā |
pauṣpiñjiśiṣyāstadbhadaiḥ saṃhitā bahūlīkṛtāḥ || 6 ||

items.text:
हिरण्यनाभशिष्यश्च चतुर्विशंतिसंहिताः ।
प्रोवाच कृतिनामासौ शिष्येभ्यः स महामतिः ।। ७ ।।
items.tr:
hiraṇyanābhaśiṣyaśca caturviśaṃtisaṃhitāḥ |
provāca kṛtināmāsau śiṣyebhyaḥ sa mahāmatiḥ || 7 ||

items.text:
तैश्वापि सामवेदोऽसौ शाखाभिकर्बहुलीकृतः ।
अथर्वणामथो वक्ष्ये संहितानां समुज्वयम् ।। ८ ।।
items.tr:
taiśvāpi sāmavedo'sau śākhābhikarbahulīkṛtaḥ |
atharvaṇāmatho vakṣye saṃhitānāṃ samujvayam || 8 ||

items.text:
शिष्यमध्यापयामास कबन्धं सोऽपि तं द्रिधा ।
कृता तु देवदर्शाय तथा पथ्याय दत्तवान् ।। ९ ।।
items.tr:
śiṣyamadhyāpayāmāsa kabandhaṃ so'pi taṃ dridhā |
kṛtā tu devadarśāya tathā pathyāya dattavān || 9 ||

items.text:
अथर्ववेदं स मुनिः सुमन्तुरमितद्युतिः ।
देवदर्शस्य शिष्यास्तु मौदगो ब्रह्मबलिस्तथा ।
शौक्यायनिः पिप्पलादस्तथान्यो मुनिसत्तमः ।। १० ।।
items.tr:
atharvavedaṃ sa muniḥ sumanturamitadyutiḥ |
devadarśasya śiṣyāstu maudago brahmabalistathā |
śaukyāyaniḥ pippalādastathānyo munisattamaḥ || 10 ||

items.text:
पथ्यस्यापि त्रयः शिष्याः कूता यैर्द्रिज! संहिताः ।
तजाजालिः कुमुदादिश्व तृतीयः शौनको द्रिज ।। ११ ।।
items.tr:
pathyasyāpi trayaḥ śiṣyāḥ kūtā yairdrija! saṃhitāḥ |
tajājāliḥ kumudādiśva tṛtīyaḥ śaunako drija || 11 ||

items.text:
शौनकस्तु द्रिधा कृत्वा ददावेकन्तु बभ्रवे ।
द्रितीयां संहिता प्रादात् सौन्धवायनसंज्ञिने ।। १२ ।।
items.tr:
śaunakastu dridhā kṛtvā dadāvekantu babhrave |
dritīyāṃ saṃhitā prādāt saundhavāyanasaṃjñine || 12 ||

items.text:
सैन्धवा मूञ्जिकेशाश्व द्रिधा भिन्नास्त्रिधा पुनः ।
नक्षत्रकल्पो वेदानां संहितानां तथैव च ।। १३ ।।
items.tr:
saindhavā mūñjikeśāśva dridhā bhinnāstridhā punaḥ |
nakṣatrakalpo vedānāṃ saṃhitānāṃ tathaiva ca || 13 ||

items.text:
चतुर्थः स्यादाङ्गिरसः शान्तिकल्पश्व पञ्चमः
श्रेष्ठास्त्वथर्वणामेते संहितानां विकल्पकाः ।। १४ ।।
items.tr:
caturthaḥ syādāṅgirasaḥ śāntikalpaśva pañcamaḥ
śreṣṭhāstvatharvaṇāmete saṃhitānāṃ vikalpakāḥ || 14 ||

items.text:
आख्यानेश्चाप्युपाख्यानैर्गाथाभिः कल्पसिद्धिभिः ।
पुराणसंहितां चक्र पुराणार्थविशारदः ।। १५ ।।
items.tr:
ākhyāneścāpyupākhyānairgāthābhiḥ kalpasiddhibhiḥ |
purāṇasaṃhitāṃ cakra purāṇārthaviśāradaḥ || 15 ||

items.text:
प्रख्यातो व्यासशिष्योऽभूत् सूतो वै रोमहर्षणः ।
पुराणसंहितां तस्मै ददौ व्यासो महामुनिः ।। १६ ।।
items.tr:
prakhyāto vyāsaśiṣyo'bhūt sūto vai romaharṣaṇaḥ |
purāṇasaṃhitāṃ tasmai dadau vyāso mahāmuniḥ || 16 ||

items.text:
सुमतिश्चाग्रिवर्जाश्च मित्रायुः शांशपायनः ।
अकृतव्रणः सावर्णिः षट् शिष्यास्तस्य चाभवन् ।। १७ ।।
items.tr:
sumatiścāgrivarjāśca mitrāyuḥ śāṃśapāyanaḥ |
akṛtavraṇaḥ sāvarṇiḥ ṣaṭ śiṣyāstasya cābhavan || 17 ||

items.text:
काश्यपः संहिताकर्ता सावर्णिः शाशपायनः ।
रोमहर्षणिका चान्या तिसृणां मूलसंहिताः ।। १८ ।।
items.tr:
kāśyapaḥ saṃhitākartā sāvarṇiḥ śāśapāyanaḥ |
romaharṣaṇikā cānyā tisṛṇāṃ mūlasaṃhitāḥ || 18 ||

items.text:
चतुष्टयेनाप्येतेन संहितानामिदं मुने ।
आद्यं सर्वपुराणानां पुराणं ब्राह्ममुच्यते ।। १९ ।।
items.tr:
catuṣṭayenāpyetena saṃhitānāmidaṃ mune |
ādyaṃ sarvapurāṇānāṃ purāṇaṃ brāhmamucyate || 19 ||

items.text:
अष्टादश पुराणानि पुराणज्ञाः प्रचक्षते ।
ब्राह्मं पाद्मं वैष्णवञ्च शैवं भागवतं तथा ।। २० ।।
items.tr:
aṣṭādaśa purāṇāni purāṇajñāḥ pracakṣate |
brāhmaṃ pādmaṃ vaiṣṇavañca śaivaṃ bhāgavataṃ tathā || 20 ||

items.text:
अथान्यन्नारदीयञ्च मार्कण्डेयञ्च सप्तमम् ।
आग्नेयमष्टमञ्चैव भविष्यं नवमं तथा ।। २१ ।।
items.tr:
athānyannāradīyañca mārkaṇḍeyañca saptamam |
āgneyamaṣṭamañcaiva bhaviṣyaṃ navamaṃ tathā || 21 ||

items.text:
दशमं ब्रह्मवैवर्तं लैङ्गमेकादशं स्मृतम् ।
वाराहं द्वादशञ्चैव स्कान्दञ्चात्र त्रयोदशम् ।। २२ ।।
items.tr:
daśamaṃ brahmavaivartaṃ laiṅgamekādaśaṃ smṛtam |
vārāhaṃ dvādaśañcaiva skāndañcātra trayodaśam || 22 ||

items.text:
चतुर्दशं वामनञ्च कौर्मं पञ्चदशं स्मृतम् ।
मात्स्यञ्च गारुड़ञ्चैव ब्रह्माण्डञ्च ततः परम ।। २३ ।।
items.tr:
caturdaśaṃ vāmanañca kaurmaṃ pañcadaśaṃ smṛtam |
mātsyañca gāruṛañcaiva brahmāṇḍañca tataḥ parama || 23 ||

items.text:
तथा चोपपुराणानि मुनिभिः कथितानि च ।
महापुराणान्येतानि ह्मष्टादश महामुने ।। २४ ।।
items.tr:
tathā copapurāṇāni munibhiḥ kathitāni ca |
mahāpurāṇānyetāni hmaṣṭādaśa mahāmune || 24 ||

items.text:
सर्गश्च प्रतिसर्गश्च वंशो मन्वन्तराणि च ।
सर्वेष्वेतेषु कथ्यन्ते वंशामनुचरितञ्च यत् ।। २५ ।।
items.tr:
sargaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca |
sarveṣveteṣu kathyante vaṃśāmanucaritañca yat || 25 ||

items.text:
यदेतत् तव मैत्रेय! पुराणां कथ्यते मया।
एतदू वैष्णवसंज्ञ वै पाह्मस्य समनन्तरम् ।। २६ ।।
items.tr:
yadetat tava maitreya! purāṇāṃ kathyate mayā|
etadū vaiṣṇavasaṃjña vai pāhmasya samanantaram || 26 ||

items.text:
सर्गे च प्रतिसर्गे च वंशमन्वन्तरादिषु ।
कथ्यते भगवान् विष्णुरशेषेष्वेव सत्तम ।। २७ ।।
items.tr:
sarge ca pratisarge ca vaṃśamanvantarādiṣu |
kathyate bhagavān viṣṇuraśeṣeṣveva sattama || 27 ||

items.text:
अह्गानि चतुरो वेदा मीमांसा न्यायविस्तरः ।
पुराणां धर्मशास्त्रञ्च विद्या ह्म ताश्चतुर्दश ।। २८ ।।
items.tr:
ahgāni caturo vedā mīmāṃsā nyāyavistaraḥ |
purāṇāṃ dharmaśāstrañca vidyā hma tāścaturdaśa || 28 ||

items.text:
आयुर्वेदो धनुर्वेदो गान्धर्वश्चैव ते त्रयः ।
अर्थशास्त्र चतुर्थन्तु विद्या ह्मष्टादशैव ताः ।। २९ ।।
items.tr:
āyurvedo dhanurvedo gāndharvaścaiva te trayaḥ |
arthaśāstra caturthantu vidyā hmaṣṭādaśaiva tāḥ || 29 ||

items.text:
ज्ञेया ब्रह्मर्षयः पूर्व तेभ्यो देवर्षयः पुनः ।
राजर्षयः पुनस्तेभ्य ऋषिप्रकृतयस्त्रयः ।। ३० ।।
items.tr:
jñeyā brahmarṣayaḥ pūrva tebhyo devarṣayaḥ punaḥ |
rājarṣayaḥ punastebhya ṛṣiprakṛtayastrayaḥ || 30 ||

items.text:
इति शाखाः प्रसंख्याताः शाखाभदास्तथैव च ।
कर्तारश्चैव शाखानां बेदहेतुस्तथोदितः ।। ३१ ।।
items.tr:
iti śākhāḥ prasaṃkhyātāḥ śākhābhadāstathaiva ca |
kartāraścaiva śākhānāṃ bedahetustathoditaḥ || 31 ||

items.text:
सर्वमन्वन्तरेष्वेव शाखाभेदाः समाः समृताः ।
प्राजापत्या श्रुतिनित्या तद्रिकल्पास्त्विमे द्रिज ।। ३२ ।।
items.tr:
sarvamanvantareṣveva śākhābhedāḥ samāḥ samṛtāḥ |
prājāpatyā śrutinityā tadrikalpāstvime drija || 32 ||

items.text:
एतत् तवोदितं सर्वं यत् पृष्टोऽहमिह त्वया ।
मैत्रेय! वेदसम्बद्ध किमन्यत् तथामि ते ।। ३३ ।।
items.tr:
etat tavoditaṃ sarvaṃ yat pṛṣṭo'hamiha tvayā |
maitreya! vedasambaddha kimanyat tathāmi te || 33 ||

en_chapter: Parāçara said:—Hear O Maitreya, how Jaimini, the pupil of Vyāsa, divided the branches of Sama-Veda. The son of Jarmini was Sumanta whose son was Sukarman. They both studied the same Sanhita under Jaimini. The latter composed Sahasra Sanhita which he gave to his two pupils named Hiranyanabha, otherwise named Kausalya and Paushyinji. Fifteen pupils of the latter composed as many Sanhitas and they were called the northern chanters of Sāman. Hiranyanabha had as many disciples who were called the eastern chanters of Sāman. Lokakshmi, Kuthami, Kushidi and Langali were the pupils of Paushyinji; and by them and their disciples many other branches were made. There was another learned disciple of Hiranyanābha by name Kriti who gave twenty-four Sanhitas to as many pupils; who again divided Sama-Veda into various branches.

I will now give you an account of the various branches of Atharva-Veda. The highly illustrious ascetic Sumanta taught this Veda to his pupil Kabandha who divided it into two and gave them to Devadersa and Pathya. The disciples of Devadersa were Mandga, Brahmabali, Saulkāyani and Pippalāda. Pathya had three disciples, Jājali, Kumudādi and Saunaka to whom were severally given three Sanhitās. Saunaka divided his Sanhitā into two and gave them to his disciples Babhru and Saindhavāyan and from them originated two schools the Saindhavas and Munjakesas. The Sanhitās of the Atharva-Veda are divided into five Kalpas or ceremonials; namely Nakshatra Kalpa or rules for worshipping the planets; the Vaitāna Kalpa or rules for oblations; the Sanhitā Kalpa or rules for sacrifices; the Angirasa Kalpa or incantations and prayers for the destruction of enemies; the Sānti Kalpa—or prayers for averting evil.

The glorious Veda-Vyāsa, conversant with the knowledge of Purānas, composed a Paurānik Sanhitā consisting of historical and legendary traditions, prayers and hymns and sacred chronology. He had a distinguished pupil Suta, who was otherwise named Romaharshana, to whom he gave the Purānas. Suta had six disciples, Sumati, Agnivarchas, Mitrayu, Sānsapāyana, Akritavrana, who is otherwise called Kāsyapa and Sāverni. The last three composed three principal Sanhitas and Romaharsana himself compiled a fourth, which is named (after him) Romaharshanika. The substance of these four Sanhitas is embodied in this Vishnu-Purāna.

Brāhma is the first of all the Purānas. Those who are conversant with the knowledge of Purānas enumerate them as eighteen—Brāhma, Padma, Vaishnava, Saiva, Bhāgvata, Nāradya, Mārkandeya, Ageney, Bhavishyat, Brahmā Vaivartta, Lainga, Varāha, Skanda, Vāmana, Kaurmma, Matsya, Gārura, Brahmānda, The creation of the universe and its successive generations, the genealogies of patriarchs and kings, the Manwantaras, and the royal dynasties are described in the Purānas. The Purāna, which I have described to you, O Maitreya, is Vaishnava and is next to Padma. And in every part, in the creation of universe and the successive generations, in the description of the genealogies of the patriarchs it has declared the glory of the great Vishnu. There are fourteen principal kinds of knowledge—namely, the four Vedas, the six Angas, the Mimānsa (theology,) Nyāya (logic,) Dharma (the institutes of law) and the Purānas. And they are enumerated as eighteen with the addition of these four—Aur-Veda, medical science taught by Dhunwantari; Dhanur-veda, the science of archery, taught by Bhrigu; Ghāndharba-Veda, the art of music, dancing &c. of which the Muni Bharata was the author; and the Artha Sastram or the science of Government, taught by Vrihaspati.

There are three orders of Rishis—the royal Rishis or princes who have devoted themselves to devotion as Viswamitra; divine Rishis or demi-gods, as Nārada; and Brahman Rishis, who are the sons of Brahmā as Vasishtha and others.

I have thus related to you the various branches of the Vedas and their sub-divisions, the persons by whom they made and the object with which they were ushered into existence. Such was the division in all the Manwantaras. The primitive Veda, which was instituted by Brahmā at the beginning of Kalpa, is eternal; these branches are but its modifications.
I have thus related to you, Maitreya, the Vedas which you desired to hear. What else do you wish to hear now?
